title: Design System: Shaun Alonzo — Independent Engineering Practice

display.purpose: Problem-led hero; desktop clamp, with explicit tablet/mobile overrides in DESIGN.md.

display-close.purpose: Muted, smaller block inside the hero heading; em is relative to its parent display.

headline.purpose: Balanced homepage section titles, not a metadata or eyebrow role.

title.purpose: Default H3 for compact offers and AI stories; process and workflow carry local overrides.

work-title.purpose: Responsive title beside a work frame; 1.5rem at tablet and 1.3125rem at narrow mobile.

concept-title.purpose: Responsive headline inside shared conceptual media; 1.25rem at tablet and 1.375rem at narrow mobile.

concept-label.purpose: Strong node title; remains at least 12px at tablet/mobile widths.

concept-detail.purpose: Selectable supporting node text at 12px; not an old miniature diagram label.

case-display.purpose: Opening title on a real static case document.

case-section.purpose: Left-column reading label for the problem, decision, scope, and outcomes.

profile-display.purpose: Engineering profile identity, with smaller mobile and print sizes.

body.purpose: Baseline prose, with a 70ch paragraph measure.

body-compact.purpose: Desktop service, work, AI, and case descriptions.

body-small.purpose: Approach descriptions, profile role summaries, and narrow compact reading text.

label.purpose: Filled/outlined button text; text-link line-height inherits from its context.

navigation.purpose: Desktop section navigation; expanded mobile links use 1rem.

metadata.purpose: Plain inline technology lists, portrait caption, and case categories.

metadata-small.purpose: Evidence classification, work categories, and footer; not reading prose.

caption.purpose: Existing employer label/disclaimer only; not the shared media caption role.

media-caption.purpose: 12px factual caption below a shared frame, with 1.6 line-height. Review-slot notes also use 12px.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Source --ease for CSS transitions and matching tracked Web Animations; the migration requestAnimationFrame timeline advances linearly.

motion.name: state-duration
motion.purpose: Button background, workflow selection fill, and text-link arrow transitions.

motion.name: link-arrow-response
motion.purpose: Only the arrow moves on text-link hover; cards and buttons do not lift.

motion.name: node-entrance
motion.purpose: Legacy non-orchestration workflow fallback only; not used on the current homepage. Orchestration boxes never move. No automatic hero entrance, scroll reveal, or hover-triggered movement.

motion.name: node-state
motion.purpose: Conceptual node background and foreground transitions.

motion.name: selection-feedback
motion.purpose: Brief finite feedback when a workflow stage is manually selected.

motion.name: anchor-scroll
motion.purpose: Native section navigation; restored entry/history targets use immediate scrolling.

motion.name: migration-timeline
motion.purpose: Pure clamped build → check → share → retire model in src/migration-state.js. Old serves during build/check; checked replacement receives no customer traffic until Share; Retire sends all traffic to the new system and turns the old off.

motion.name: migration-traffic
motion.purpose: Elapsed is milliseconds; weight > 0 makes a route visible. SVG connections change, never HTML box positions. Stroke weights are illustrative, not measured traffic or visible rollout metrics.

motion.name: migration-share-weights
motion.purpose: Share-stage animation parameters only. Replacement weight is 0 during Build/Check and 1 during Retire; both systems serve throughout Share. No percentages, counters, or live-status claims are shown.

motion.name: migration-build-progress
motion.purpose: Thin replacement-build rule driven by the pure frame's buildProgress; hidden outside Build. This transform never moves or scales a system box.

motion.name: migration-playback
motion.value: one active controller; autoplay once at visibility ≥ 0.55; pause below 0.1 or document.hidden; no autoresume; no loop
motion.purpose: src/migration.js coordinates the modernization work/case frames. The hero now uses a supplied Redbook gallery. Pause/Play/Replay are explicit; stage selection pauses and consumes one-time autoplay. No new preference is persisted.

motion.name: orchestration-handoffs
motion.value: finite selectable build or conditional research/re-plan route; fixed HTML nodes; SVG handoffs
motion.purpose: src/agent-workflow-state.js and src/agent-workflow.js send every specialist result through the Sonnet orchestrator, with Claude Opus planning and optional Sonnet / Opus research, ending at developer approval. Pause/Play/Replay, static stage selection, offscreen/background pause without autoresume, reduced-motion and no-JavaScript alternatives; never live execution.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: scroll-behavior: auto; animation: none !important; transition: none !important
motion.purpose: Global CSS reduction; JS cancels tracked Web Animations and pauses migration on reduced-motion/background changes. Reduced motion hides AI replay and migration transport, shows the migration explanation, and retains static stage selection. No-JavaScript migration keeps the complete written four-step sequence.

motion.name: video-playback
motion.value: manual; no autoplay; no loop; preload: none
motion.purpose: Native controls, poster, and playsinline; pause offscreen/background without autoresume. Transcript always required; meaningful audio requires captions.

components.name: Shared Migration Frame
components.description: Static selected Check snapshot of the modernization work/.NET-case frame: fixed HTML customers/router/old/new nodes, SVG connections, old serving, replacement ready/checked with no customer traffic. The hero now displays Redbook screenshots. Self-contained visual preview only: no animation, transport controls, or wired stage selection. Source src/migration-state.js and src/migration.js supply the finite 14.4s sequence, one-time visible autoplay, explicit playback/stage controls, and reduced-motion/no-JavaScript fallbacks; approved media replaces it normally. Agent orchestration is separate.

components.name: Supplied Screenshot Gallery
components.description: Native labeled screenshot figures with full-size local links, meaningful alternatives, intrinsic dimensions, and uncropped pixels. Redbook desktop/mobile is reused in the hero and case, not repeated in its homepage work entry; Cards Guide PH uses a paired mobile gallery with native narrow-screen horizontal scrolling. Source assets and limitations are recorded in public/assets/work/SOURCES.md; original inputs are unchanged. No generated composite or fake device chrome.

components.name: Copy Email Control
components.description: Borderless contact utility and reserved live-status space. Actual clipboard/busy/feedback behavior is supplied by src/contact.js, not embedded in this visual snippet.
components.css: .ds-copy-context { color: var(--proof-ink, #174d3e); font-family: var(--font, Manrope, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-copy { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 0; background: transparent; border: 0; min-height: 44px; color: inherit; font: 600 0.8125rem/1.75 var(--font, Manrope, system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; touch-action: manipulation; } .ds-copy svg { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-copy:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-copy:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #006b57); outline-offset: 5px; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-copy:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.6; } .ds-copy-status { display: block; visibility: hidden; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.75; margin-top: 7px; min-height: 1.7em; } .ds-copy-status.ds-show { visibility: visible; } @media (max-width: 600px) { .ds-copy { font-size: 0.75rem; } }

narrative.overview:
A calm, client-first engineering practice expressed as a visual decision brief: cool white, deep green ink, controlled teal, and confident Manrope headings. Large media frames, aligned conceptual geometry, open rows, and crisp rules make the work understandable before asking for extended reading. Expression comes from composition, with finite movement explaining the approved migration handover or deliberate AI workflow selection and replay, not ornamental effects.

The same visual identity supports practical AI, software delivery, and the full-time hiring path. Professional work, personal experiments, and illustrative workflows remain visibly distinct. Semantic conceptual frames stand in honestly until approved screenshots or recordings are supplied; they are not fabricated product evidence or live activity. This is a code-led extension of the existing world, with no generated comp or imagery; the user-supplied portrait is reused without visual changes.
keyCharacteristics: Light-led green neutrals with a complete dark-theme counterpart.
One self-hosted variable family, large left-aligned headings, and compact contextual metadata.
Alternating media/copy rows, compact summaries, thin dividers, and flat tinted frames.
Filled email actions, quieter text links, and native document navigation.
Semantic conceptual geometry, explicitly scoped evidence, and a manually explorable workflow.
Visible-by-default content, fixed diagram boxes, one-pass traffic and agent handoffs, conditional research/re-planning, supplied screenshot galleries, and reduced-motion parity.

rules.name: The Evidence Pair Rule
rules.body: Tinted evidence and inquiry fields always use their paired ink; dark AI evidence uses its own foreground and divider colors.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Use Manrope for headings, prose, navigation, and technical context; hierarchy comes from scale, weight, measure, and spacing rather than another display face.

rules.name: The Flat Brief Rule
rules.body: Separate content with whitespace, tonal fields, and thin rules, not shadows, glows, or lifted card shells.

rules.name: The Fixed Systems Rule
rules.body: Migration motion changes SVG traffic and build progress, never box positions; other conceptual diagrams stay still on hover, with no automatic hero entrance or endless loop.

dos: Do keep the light-led green identity and verify its paired dark-theme values.
Do use the filled email action and quieter native links without intercepting ordinary history.
Do keep diagrams semantic, conceptual, and explicitly distinguished from private production artifacts.
Do preserve open rows, thin dividers, and the modest container/button corner relationship.
Do keep keyboard outlines, no-JavaScript reading, reduced-motion behavior, and printable profile rules intact.
Do keep supporting metadata subordinate without using it as the size for new reading copy.
Do let conceptual frames grow to fit their content and contain real media without cropping interface text.
Do keep motion finite, optional, and secondary to visible text; use the approved one-pass migration handover and explicit AI workflow selection/replay.
donts: Don't reintroduce the superseded navy/mint Inter console, pill chips, floating chat, or hover-lift card system.
Don't add glows, gradients, stock illustrations, generated compositions, or decorative architecture graphics to this visual world.
Don't turn offer summaries and ordinary evidence into a uniform boxed-card grid.
Don't imply a backend form, scheduler, downloadable résumé, new metric, or unsupported evidence through interface design.
Don't mistake conceptual geometry, replay, or controlled media fixtures for a screenshot, live agent activity, or measured result.
Don't treat `publish: false` or a LAN review as confidentiality or publication approval.
